subject: MSA & Order Form — term length, auto-renew opt-out, and convenience termination
messages:
From: Priya Shah <priya@acme-analytics.com>
To: dylan_brooks <dylan_brooks@redwood.com>, lauren_bishop <lauren_bishop@redwood.com>
Cc: contracts@acme-analytics.com
Date: Sat, 28 Mar 2026 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: MSA + Order Form: initial redlines and a few Qs

Hi Dylan / Lauren,

Thanks again for the productive demo last week. The procurement team reviewed the draft MSA and Order Form and attached a set of redlines (Acme_MSA_Redlines_v3.docx) plus a short summary of asks (Redline_Summary_vs_Redwood.xlsx).

The items that are blocking approval on our side are:
- Auto-renew: we prefer explicit opt-in rather than automatic renewal after the initial term, or at minimum a 90-day notice window to opt out.
- Term length & notice: propose 12 month initial term with 60-day non-renewal notice (your draft had 12 months + 30 days).
- Termination for convenience: we request mutual 30-day termination for convenience with pro-rated refunds for unused committed capacity.

Could you confirm which of these are negotiable from your side? We flagged the redlines that correspond to the clauses above.

Also attaching the partially-completed supplier security questionnaire — our legal will need a few evidence items before signing (SOC 2 cert and one-page data retention statement).

Attachments: Acme_MSA_Redlines_v3.docx, OrderForm_Acme_v2.pdf, Redline_Summary_vs_Redwood.xlsx

Best,
Priya Shah
Head of Procurement
Acme Analytics


From: dylan_brooks <dylan_brooks@redwood.com>
To: Priya Shah <priya@acme-analytics.com>
Cc: lauren_bishop <lauren_bishop@redwood.com>, priyom_das <priyom_das@redwood.com>
Date: Mon, 30 Mar 2026 10:03:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: MSA + Order Form: initial redlines and a few Qs

Hi Priya — thanks for sending this over and for the clear summary. I glanced through the redline highlights and pulled in Lauren (sales ops) and Priyom (legal) to confirm our position and next steps. A few quick notes from a commercial standpoint: 

- 12 month initial term is fine.
- We try to avoid auto-renew opt-in requirements because they can cause production discontinuity; however, we can agree to a longer opt-out window (60–90 days) for enterprise deals.
- Termination for convenience is more sensitive because of reserved capacity — we may need to preserve a notice and potential early termination fee for committed Dedicated capacity. For hosted usage-only deals the economics are simpler.

Priyom — can you review the redlines (esp. sections 4–6 re: Term / Renewal / Termination) and propose language that balances Acme's request for mutuality with our capacity commitments? Lauren, can you confirm whether this deal will include Dedicated capacity on the Order Form or if it's hosted only? That affects the refund calculation.

Priya — we'll aim to get back with proposed counter-language by end of day Wednesday. If it helps, happy to set a short call to resolve the notice window and refund calculation in one go.

Cheers,
Dylan
Senior Account Executive, Redwood Inference
From: priyom_das <priyom_das@redwood.com>
To: dylan_brooks <dylan_brooks@redwood.com>, lauren_bishop <lauren_bishop@redwood.com>
Cc: Priya Shah <priya@acme-analytics.com>
Date: Wed, 01 Apr 2026 09:18:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: MSA & Order Form — term length, auto-renew opt-out, and convenience termination

Hi all — reviewed Acme's redlines and Dylan's summary. Attached is a short counter-proposal and inline clause suggestions (see OrderForm_Acme_v2.pdf with comments and attached snippet text in the drive link). High level position: 

1) Auto-renew: we can accept a 60-day non-renew notice period for enterprise deals (document the notification window and playbook for automatic invoice stop). We will not shift to an opt-in model by default — operationally risky for customers in production.

2) Notice windows: 12 month initial term + 60-day non-renew notice accepted. We will add explicit calendar-day definition and a clause that allows Redwood to set an alternate notice timeline for Dedicated capacity after a customer change request (to protect scheduled provisioning).

3) Termination for convenience: propose mutual 90-day notice if the Order Form includes Dedicated (reserved) capacity; for hosted-only (no reserved throughput), mutual 30-day termination with pro-rated refunds for pre-paid credits. The logic is: reserved capacity has provisioning and financial commitments that require a longer runway.

4) Refunds: pro-rated refunds for prepaid, non-consumable capacity; apply any early-termination charge to committed Dedicated monthly base. We'll include worked examples in the Order Form appendix so Acme can see the math.

Action items:
- Dylan / Lauren: confirm whether Acme's Order Form includes Dedicated capacity line items (SKU IDs attached).
- Dylan: propose scheduling a 30-min alignment call with Acme legal this week — I can join.
- Priya (Acme): please confirm whether you need us to accept any language that changes the auto-renew default behavior (i.e., explicit opt-in) or if a 60-day opt-out window will suffice.

Attachments referenced: OrderForm_Acme_v2.pdf (with comments).

Thanks,
Priyom Das
Senior Counsel, Redwood Inference
From: Priya Shah <priya@acme-analytics.com>

Subject: Re: MSA & Order Form — term length, auto-renew opt-out, and convenience termination

Thanks Priyom / Dylan — that approach makes sense and is closer to what our procurement/legal can accept. A couple of clarifications before we proceed to signatures:

- Acme will accept a 60-day non-renew notice (instead of opt-in) as long as the Order Form contains a clear notification process and a calendar definition.
- For Dedicated capacity, the mutual 90-day termination is acceptable provided you include a worked example of the early termination charge and a pro-rata refund model for any unused committed credits.
- On refunds: we'd like the worked example to show monthly proration and how unused prepaid credits are calculated; a short appendix in the Order Form will be sufficient.

If you can produce the revised Order Form (preferably a tracked PDF) and send a DocuSign link, we can aim to sign next week.

Drive: https://drive.google.com/open?id=1a2b3cAcmeMSARedlines

Looking forward to wrapping this up.

Best,
